text: Self-improvement cycle 5: preserve actual usage in benchmark budget failures
description: Observed limitation from the invalid v2 live run: five adapter errors said only `exceeded registered budget`, losing whether tokens, wall time, or both crossed their limits and by how much. Add a shared deterministic budget-error formatter used by both Codex autonomy adapters. Its error must report actual/limit token and millisecond values and explicitly name each exceeded dimension, while retaining fail-closed behavior and never converting the failed run into admissible evidence. Add boundary tests for token-only, time-only, both, and exact-limit acceptance; run the full package suite, TypeScript, and diff checks. Do not rerun the invalid experiment.

reflections.context: Five v2 confirmatory runs were correctly rejected but their generic budget messages discarded the authoritative overrun dimension and magnitude.
reflections.outcome: Added shared assertCodexBenchmarkBudget used by both v1 and v2 adapters. It accepts exact limits and reports actual/limit values for token-only, wall-time-only, and dual overruns while still throwing and excluding the run. Added four boundary assertions. Verification: 118/118 tests, tsc --noEmit, and git diff --check pass. The invalid v2 experiment was not rerun.
reflections.effectiveness: Future invalid experiments retain actionable resource evidence without weakening budgets or admissibility. Existing adapter error handling remains compatible because messages retain the registered-budget marker.
reflections.lesson: Fail-closed evidence should still be information-rich; rejection and diagnostic preservation are complementary.
reflections.pattern: Centralize resource-boundary checks so experimental adapters cannot drift in acceptance or error detail.

supportingConnections.explanation: Uses improved actual/limit diagnostics if calibration caps are exceeded.

status.comment: Budget diagnostics hardened across both autonomy adapters and fully verified; awaiting user acceptance.

valueRationale: Diagnostic completeness allows invalid experiments to inform future preregistration without rerunning or weakening fail-closed evidence rules.
